title: Atlas relationship record
description: One typed, directed edge between two canonical entity records. Status: accepted (S04 human review, 2026-09-30; D-028 to D-033). This file is the one home of the record shape, the relation-type vocabulary and each type's endpoint types. Why each type exists, its level, its evidence expectation and what it must not be confused with are in docs/architecture/relationship-taxonomy.md. Shared shapes (claim IDs, partial dates, entity ID patterns, assertions, explicit states) are referenced from entities.schema.json, never copied.

source_entity.description: The subject of the sentence '<source> <relation_type> <target>'. Its allowed types depend on relation_type.

target_entity.description: The object of the sentence. Its allowed types depend on relation_type.

claim_ids.description: Claims that support the edge itself (D-028). Claim type and evidence status live on the claim (S06). There is no record-level source_ids.

valid_from.description: Start of the period the cited claims support. Left out when the claims give no period. Instance-level types only.

valid_to.description: End of the period the cited claims support. Left out when the claims give no end; that is not a claim that the edge is current.

item.description: supplies only: what is supplied. Part of what the edge says, so it is supported by the record's claim_ids.

supplier.description: incorporates only: who supplies the part, as assertions with their own claims, or an explicit state (D-031).

rel_requires.description: Class level. Endpoints are vendor-neutral classes; no time bounds (a time-bound statement is contingent and belongs at instance level).

rel_has_part.description: Class level. Whole class to part class; both constituent components (checked by validate-data).

rel_owns.description: Instance level. Controlling ownership of a company or a site.

rel_operates.description: Instance level. Running a site, which may differ from owning it (S09 distinction).

rel_designs.description: Instance level. A named company performs the design of a named product. Never a class target: what a firm does in general is a role (D-024).

rel_fabricates.description: Instance level. Wafer fabrication of a named product's dies. No process qualifier: the process as the vendor names it lives in product.vendor_process_name (one home).

rel_packages.description: Instance level. Assembly and packaging of a named product, including 2.5D integration and HBM die stacking. No vendor-named packaging-process qualifier in v1 (D-032).

rel_incorporates.description: Instance level. A named product physically contains a part: a component class, or a named product. When the part is a named product its supplier is that product's vendor, so supplier must be not_applicable (one home).

rel_supplies.description: Instance level. Company-level supply: the source sells the item to the target company. Recorded only from a claim stated at company level; never derived from product-level supplier values.

rel_houses.description: Instance level. Units of a named hardware product are installed and run at a named data-centre facility. No count: counts are metrics (NG-11) and usually non-public.

rel_provides_access_to.description: Instance level. A named service product gives its users access to a named hardware product.

not_placeholder.description: An endpoint names a real, identified record. A placeholder such as company-unknown-supplier would turn 'not recorded' into a fake entity (D-028). An unknown supplier is an explicit state (D-031).

endpoint_any.description: Any instantiable entity type that some relation type uses. Jurisdiction is deliberately absent: location, incorporation and headquarters are entity fields (D-030). Reserved types and record kinds are never endpoints (D-028).

attr_supplier.description: D-025 attribute contract applied to one edge qualifier: a non-empty list of company assertions, each with its own claims (several = multi-sourcing), or an explicit state. not_publicly_determinable must cite the claims that show it.

vocab_relation_type.description: Relation types adopted in v1 (D-029). Generic verbs (associated_with, related_to, uses, depends_on, ...), stored inverses (fabricated_by, part_of, ...), taxonomic verbs (is_a, instance_of, ...) and policy or energy verbs are deliberately absent, so records using them fail here. x-level is class or instance; x-deps lists the domain-map dependencies the type covers; x-inverse-reading is display text only, never a stored type.

oneOf.description: Making or operating any instance of the source class is not possible, at the state of technology the cited source describes, without the target class. Necessity, not current practice.
Every instance of the source component class physically contains an instance of the target component class, by the class's technical definition (e.g. an HBM stack has a base die, HBM-03).
The source company holds controlling ownership of the target company or facility, as the cited source states it (e.g. a subsidiary). A minority stake is not owns; an investment is an event.
The source company runs the day-to-day activity of the target facility. Says nothing about who owns it.
The source company performs design work on the target product (a chip or system). Not established by the product's vendor field alone.
The source company performs wafer fabrication of the target product's dies (front end, including TSV formation). Not packaging, not design.

The source company performs assembly and packaging of the target product after wafer fabrication: dicing, die stacking, 2.5D integration on an interposer, and steps such as TSV reveal. Package test is not included (future scope).
The source product physically contains the target: a constituent component class, or a named product. The supplier of a class-level part is the edge's supplier qualifier.
The source company sells or licenses the item (a product or a component class) to the target company, as a claim states at company level.
Units of the target hardware product are installed and run at the source data-centre facility.
The source service product lets its users run workloads on the target hardware product, as the provider's documentation states.
